name: Ably
why: Managed pub/sub with presence and history
cons: Priced per message and connection; costs climb quickly with high fan-out

name: Adyen
why: Enterprise-grade acquirer with unified commerce

attrs.note: Interchange plus a processing fee, not included

cons: Enterprise onboarding and minimum volumes; heavier integration than Stripe

name: Algolia
why: Hosted search with best-in-class relevance; pricey at scale
cons: Priced per search request and record; expensive at high query volume

name: Anthropic API
why: Hosted Claude models, strong at long-context and coding
cons: Per-token pricing and an external data processor; add caching and spend limits

name: Auth0
why: Best-in-class hosted identity with SSO and social
cons: Monthly active user pricing rises steeply past the free tier, especially for B2B features

name: Amazon Bedrock
why: Multiple foundation models behind one AWS API
cons: Per-token pricing; model availability varies by AWS region

name: Amazon SES
why: $0.10 per 1,000 emails, deliverability work is yours
cons: Starts in a sandbox; production access, bounce handling and domain setup are on you

name: Amazon SNS SMS
why: Cheap transactional SMS for AWS stacks, DLT registration still needed in India
cons: Per-message pricing varies by country; sender registration is needed in many markets

name: AWS WAF
why: Rule-based web filtering for CloudFront and ALB
cons: Rules need tuning to avoid blocking real users; billed per rule and per request

name: Azure Blob Storage
why: Object storage native to Azure
cons: Egress and transaction charges add up for media-heavy apps

name: Azure DevOps Pipelines
why: Pipelines with first-class Windows/.NET agents, five free users
cons: Less community tooling than GitHub Actions; parallel jobs are limited on the free tier

name: Azure DNS
why: Hosted DNS integrated with Azure
cons: No registrar; domains are bought elsewhere

name: Azure Front Door
why: CDN plus WAF integrated with Azure origins
cons: Base fee per profile makes it costly for small apps

name: Azure Machine Learning
why: Managed training and MLOps on Azure
cons: Many moving parts (workspaces, compute, registries) for a small team to learn

name: Azure Monitor / Application Insights
why: Native monitoring with strong .NET diagnostics
cons: Log ingestion is billed per GB; set sampling and retention early

name: Azure OpenAI Service
why: OpenAI models inside Azure with regional deployment and enterprise controls
cons: Quota is per region and model; capacity requests can take time

name: Azure Service Bus
why: Enterprise queues and topics for .NET/Azure
cons: Azure-only; the Premium tier needed for isolation is costly

name: Azure SignalR Service
why: Managed SignalR for ASP.NET Core
cons: Billed per unit of concurrent connections; Azure-only

name: Azure Web Application Firewall
why: WAF on Front Door or Application Gateway
cons: Needs Front Door or Application Gateway, which adds base cost

name: Backblaze B2
why: Cheapest S3-compatible storage
cons: Fewer regions and fewer integrations than the big clouds

name: Brevo
why: Free 300 emails per day, transactional and marketing
cons: Shared sending IPs on lower tiers can hurt deliverability

name: BullMQ (on Redis)
why: Job queue for Node reusing the existing Redis
cons: Needs a Redis instance that persists data; Node.js only

name: Bunny CDN
why: Very cheap pay-as-you-go delivery
cons: Smaller security and edge-compute feature set than the big CDNs

name: Cashfree Payments
why: RBI-licensed gateway with UPI and payouts

attrs.note: Transaction fee about 1.95%, not included in the infrastructure band

cons: India-focused; limited international card coverage

name: Celery (on Redis/RabbitMQ)
why: Standard Python task queue
cons: Needs a broker (Redis or RabbitMQ) and worker processes to run and monitor

name: Centrifugo
why: Self-hosted websocket server in Go, works with any backend
cons: Another server to deploy, scale and secure

name: Clerk
why: Drop-in UI components, fast to integrate for React/Next.js
cons: Monthly active user pricing; user data lives with a third-party vendor

name: Cloudflare CDN
why: Free global CDN with DDoS protection; unlimited bandwidth on free plan
cons: Advanced caching rules and features sit on paid plans

name: Cloudflare DNS
why: Free, fast authoritative DNS
cons: Works best with Cloudflare proxying, which ties traffic routing to one vendor

name: Cloudflare R2
why: S3-compatible with zero egress fees
cons: Fewer storage classes and lifecycle options than S3

name: Cloudflare WAF
why: Managed rules and bot protection from the Pro plan
cons: Managed rulesets beyond the basics need a paid plan

name: Amazon CloudFront
why: Deep AWS integration, India edge presence, 1 TB free per month
cons: Pricing varies by region; cache invalidations past the free quota are billed

name: Amazon CloudWatch
why: Native AWS metrics, logs and alarms
cons: Logs and custom metrics are billed per GB and per metric; costs creep without retention limits

name: Amazon Cognito
why: Cheap user pools with SAML/OIDC federation; clunky developer experience
cons: Customising hosted flows is limited and migrating users out is hard

name: CouchDB + PouchDB
why: Mature replication protocol, open source
cons: Document model with conflict revisions; smaller community today

name: Datadog
why: Most complete SaaS observability, expensive as you add hosts
cons: Per-host and per-GB pricing grows quickly

name: Microsoft Entra External ID
why: Customer identity on Azure with 50,000 free monthly active users
cons: Custom branding and flows take Azure-specific configuration

name: Microsoft Entra ID (workforce SSO)
why: Workforce single sign-on with conditional access; the free tier covers SSO for apps
cons: Ties sign-in to the Microsoft tenant; external users need guest setup

name: Expo Push Notifications
why: One API for FCM and APNs in Expo apps
cons: Only for Expo apps; a thin relay over APNs and FCM

name: Firebase Cloud Messaging
why: Free push for Android, iOS and web
cons: Delivery is best effort with no guaranteed timing; analytics are basic

name: Amazon SNS mobile push
why: AWS-native push fan-out to APNs and FCM device tokens, inside the AWS compliance boundary
cons: Delivers through APNs and FCM, so device tokens and app credentials for both still have to be managed
Plain delivery; segmentation, templates and analytics are built yourself

sources.title: AWS services in scope by compliance program

name: Firebase Authentication
why: Email, social and phone sign-in with good mobile SDKs
cons: No SLA on the free tier; enterprise features need Identity Platform

name: Firebase phone verification
why: OTP bundled into Firebase Authentication
cons: SMS verification is billed per message past a small free quota

name: Cloud Storage for Firebase
why: Mobile-friendly uploads with security rules
cons: Security rules are a separate language to learn and test

name: Firestore offline persistence
why: Offline cache and automatic reconciliation in the Firebase SDKs
cons: Conflicts resolve as last write wins; complex queries are limited offline

name: Drift (SQLite) + sync endpoint
why: Typed local SQLite for Flutter with a custom sync API
cons: The sync endpoint and conflict handling are yours to build

name: Formspree
why: Static-site contact forms with spam filtering, free for 50 submissions per month
cons: Monthly submission caps on the free plan

name: Framework built-in auth (sessions/JWT)
why: No external service; uses the backend framework's own session or token auth (Django auth, Laravel, ASP.NET Core Identity, Spring Security and similar)
cons: Password storage, resets, MFA and account lockout are your responsibility

name: Google Analytics 4
why: Free, ubiquitous web analytics
cons: Sampling and data retention limits; needs a cookie consent setup in the EU

name: Google Pub/Sub
why: Managed messaging with global scale
cons: At-least-once delivery, so consumers must handle duplicates

name: Google Cloud Storage
why: Durable object store with strong GCP integration
cons: Egress to the internet is billed per GB

name: Google Gemini API (Vertex AI)
why: Hosted Gemini models with GCP regional controls
cons: Per-token pricing; data use terms differ between AI Studio and Vertex AI

name: GitHub Actions
why: Workflows next to the code; the 2,000 free minutes a month cover a small team, larger teams buy extra minutes
cons: Minute limits on private repositories; long builds need paid or self-hosted runners

name: GitLab CI/CD
why: Integrated pipelines, self-managed option
cons: Compute minute limits on the free tier

name: Google Cloud DNS
why: Hosted DNS with 100% SLA
cons: Not a registrar, so domains are bought elsewhere; billed per zone

name: Grafana Cloud
why: Metrics, logs, traces on a free tier
cons: Free tier limits on metrics series and log volume

name: Jenkins
why: Self-hosted automation server for air-gapped sites
cons: A server to patch, back up and maintain plugins on

name: Apache Kafka
why: Durable high-throughput event log, heavy to run
cons: Heavy to run; partitions, retention and consumer groups need expertise

name: Keycloak
why: Open-source identity server with SSO, runs fully on-premise
cons: A Java server to run, upgrade and back up yourself

name: Liveblocks
why: Managed presence and CRDT collaboration primitives
cons: Priced per connection and room; vendor-specific data model

name: Meilisearch
why: Typo-tolerant search, simple to run (cloud from ~$30)
cons: A separate index to keep in sync with the database

name: MinIO (self-hosted)
why: S3-compatible store that runs on-premise or air-gapped
cons: Running durable storage yourself means planning disks, erasure coding and backups

name: MSG91
why: India-focused OTP and SMS with DLT support
cons: India-focused; DLT template registration is required

name: NATS JetStream
why: Lightweight single-binary messaging, good fit for Go
cons: Smaller ecosystem than Kafka; JetStream persistence needs care

name: Netlify Forms
why: Built-in forms when hosted on Netlify
cons: Only works on Netlify hosting; submission caps on the free plan

name: OneSignal
why: Dashboard and segmentation on top of FCM/APNs, free mobile push
cons: Free tier puts limits on data export and audience features

name: OpenAI API
why: Leading hosted LLMs; usage priced per token
cons: Per-token pricing and an external data processor; add caching and spend limits

name: OpenSearch / Elasticsearch
why: Full-featured search and analytics cluster, high ops
cons: A heavy cluster to size, tune and keep in sync with the database

name: PayPal Checkout
why: Widely trusted wallet and card checkout globally

attrs.note: Transaction fee about 3.5% + fixed amount, not included

cons: Higher fees and a less flexible checkout than card processors

name: pgvector
why: Vector search inside PostgreSQL, no extra service
cons: Approximate indexes need tuning; very large vector sets can strain the main database

name: Pinecone
why: Managed vector database
cons: Another vendor holding a copy of your data; billed per read and write unit

name: Plausible Analytics
why: Privacy-friendly lightweight analytics, no cookie banner needed
cons: Aggregate statistics only, no per-user funnels

name: PostgreSQL full-text search
why: Built into the database: no extra service up to moderate catalogue sizes
cons: Weaker typo tolerance and relevance tuning than a dedicated search engine; heavy queries share the database

name: PostHog
why: Product analytics, session replay, flags, free to 1M events a month
cons: Event volume pricing past the free tier; self-hosting is heavy

name: Postmark
why: High deliverability for transactional email
cons: Transactional email only; marketing email needs a separate stream

name: PowerSync
why: Offline-first SQLite sync for Postgres, MongoDB and MySQL backends
cons: Another service between the app and Postgres; sync rules to learn

name: Prometheus + Grafana (self-hosted)
why: Open-source metrics stack for on-premise
cons: You run storage, retention and alerting yourself

name: Pusher Channels
why: Simple managed websockets
cons: Connection and message caps per plan

name: Qdrant
why: Dedicated open-source vector database, cloud or self-hosted
cons: Another data store to run or pay for and keep in sync

name: RabbitMQ
why: Mature broker, self-host or CloudAMQP
cons: A broker to run, monitor and upgrade

name: Razorpay
why: RBI-licensed gateway with UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets; about 2% per transaction

attrs.note: Transaction fee about 2%, not included in the infrastructure band

cons: Mainly for Indian businesses; international payments need separate approval

name: Managed Redis/Valkey (ElastiCache, Memorystore, Azure Cache)
why: Native cloud cache with replicas and failover
cons: Memory-priced; a minimum instance costs money even when idle

name: Resend
why: Developer-friendly API, free 3,000 emails per month
cons: Newer service with a smaller feature set than older email providers

name: Room + WorkManager sync (native Android)
why: Platform-recommended offline-first pattern with a REST sync endpoint
cons: Android only; sync and conflict logic are built by hand

name: Amazon Route 53
why: Reliable DNS with health checks
cons: Billed per hosted zone and per query; AWS-specific routing features

name: Amazon S3
why: 11 nines durability, de facto object storage
cons: Egress and request charges add up for public media

name: Amazon SageMaker
why: Managed training and hosting of custom models
cons: Many concepts to learn; idle endpoints still bill

name: Twilio SendGrid
why: Established transactional email, free 100 per day
cons: Shared IPs on lower tiers; deliverability needs domain authentication

name: Sentry
why: Error tracking and performance with free developer plan
cons: Event quota per plan; sample high-volume errors

name: Amazon SQS
why: Zero-ops managed queue with pay per request
cons: AWS-only; FIFO queues have throughput limits

name: Stripe
why: Best developer experience and global coverage

attrs.note: Transaction fee about 2.9% + $0.30 in the US, not included

cons: Limited availability and UPI support for new Indian businesses
Per-transaction fees; payouts and some methods vary by country

name: Supabase Auth
why: Included with Supabase, row-level security integration
cons: Ties user accounts to the Supabase project; enterprise SSO needs a paid plan

name: Supabase Storage
why: Bundled with Supabase
cons: Tied to the Supabase project; egress counts toward plan limits

name: Twilio Verify / SMS
why: Global OTP delivery; India routes need DLT registration and cost more
cons: Per-verification pricing that varies by country

name: Typesense
why: In-memory fast search, open source, cloud or self-host
cons: A separate index to keep in sync; the whole index sits in RAM

name: Upstash Redis
why: Serverless Redis billed per request, suits functions
cons: Per-request pricing gets costly at sustained high throughput

name: UptimeRobot / Better Stack uptime checks
why: Basic uptime pings for small sites
cons: Checks reachability only, not application errors

name: Self-hosted Redis/Valkey
why: Runs next to the app on the same host with no vendor
cons: Persistence, failover and memory limits are yours to manage

name: Vertex AI (training)
why: Managed training with TPUs/GPUs
cons: Many concepts to learn; training compute is billed per hour

name: Self-hosted open models (vLLM/Ollama)
why: Fully air-gapped inference on your own GPUs
cons: Needs GPUs, model updates and capacity planning in-house

name: WatermelonDB sync
why: Local-first SQLite for React Native with a pull/push sync protocol you implement
cons: React Native only; you build the backend sync endpoints

name: Web3Forms
why: Free form endpoint for static sites
cons: Limited spam filtering and workflow options on the free plan

name: Google Cloud Identity Platform
why: Firebase Authentication with an SLA, multi-tenancy and HIPAA coverage
cons: Priced per monthly active user past the free tier; GCP-specific setup

name: GlitchTip (self-hosted)
why: Self-hosted, Sentry-compatible error tracking
cons: Self-hosted; you run the database and upgrades

name: Firestore real-time listeners
why: Built-in snapshot listeners push document changes to every connected client
cons: Billed per document read; broad listeners get expensive

name: Supabase Realtime
why: Postgres changes, broadcast and presence over WebSockets, part of the Supabase platform
cons: Concurrent connection and message limits per plan

name: WebSockets/SSE in the backend framework
why: The backend serves WebSocket or server-sent-event connections itself
cons: Sticky connections complicate scaling; fan-out across instances needs a pub/sub layer

name: Yjs with Hocuspocus
why: CRDT shared documents (Yjs) with a WebSocket sync server, so simultaneous edits merge without conflicts
cons: A dedicated collaboration server to run and persist documents from

name: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart (private model endpoint)
why: Models hosted as an endpoint inside your own AWS account, so data stays within your boundary
cons: Endpoints bill per instance hour even when idle

name: Vertex AI Model Garden (private endpoint)
why: Models hosted as an endpoint inside your own Google Cloud project
cons: Endpoints bill per node hour even when idle

name: EMQX (MQTT broker)
why: Self-hosted MQTT broker that handles millions of device connections
cons: A broker cluster to run and secure with device certificates

name: AWS IoT Core
why: Managed MQTT ingestion with device registry and rules
cons: Priced per message and connection minute; AWS-specific device model

name: Azure IoT Hub
why: Managed device-to-cloud messaging for Azure estates
cons: Unit-based tiers with daily message caps

name: Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint (small instance)
why: Hosts a tabular scoring model (gradient boosting or similar) on one or two small instances inside your own AWS account
cons: Bills per instance hour even when idle

name: Vertex AI online prediction endpoint (small machine)
why: Hosts a tabular scoring model on small machines inside your own Google Cloud project
cons: Bills per node hour even when idle; no scale to zero

name: Azure Machine Learning online endpoint (small instance)
why: Hosts a tabular scoring model on small instances inside your own Azure subscription
cons: Bills per instance hour even when idle

name: Self-hosted model server (BentoML or FastAPI with ONNX) on the app cluster
why: Serves a small scoring model next to the app with no vendor, at the price of running it yourself
cons: Model versioning, scaling and monitoring are built and run in-house
